situations.name: Recurrence editor
situations.definition: A control that lets a user author 'how often does this run' — preset chips, a raw cron field, an interval field, and a timezone — and hands back a config the scheduler will honor.
situations.owner: src/lib/utils/cronPresets.ts (presets only — no shared editor component exists)
situations.note: Four independent editors and TWO CRON_PRESETS tables (lib/utils/cronPresets vs cloudSchedulesHelpers:28); the scraper and cloud editors are bare text inputs with a hardcoded 'UTC' hint while the local ones do backend-validated preview + IANA picker.

situations.name: Next-run projection
situations.definition: Rendering the concrete future fire times a schedule will produce, so the user can confirm intent before saving.
situations.note: The hard part is honesty: a client-side `now + N*interval` walk (TriggerSchedulePreview:8) does not match the engine's `next_trigger_at`-anchored phase or its seeded cron H-token spread — useCronPreview:12 documents deleting a whole hook because it 'rendered a lie'.

situations.name: Timezone handling
situations.definition: Letting the user pick which zone a time-based rule is evaluated in, and displaying resolved times in a zone the user actually understands.
situations.note: ActiveHoursSection:230 takes IANA zones as free text while everything else uses TimezoneSelect; three different fallback chains (schedule tz → theme tz → system local) and cloud silently assumes UTC. An incident (C5-handoff-2026-04-26) is cited inline as the reason for the current defaults.

situations.name: Polymorphic config form
situations.definition: One authoring surface whose fields change completely based on a chosen kind (trigger type, binding kind, schema field type), then serializes to a single opaque config blob.
situations.note: Triggers use one flat 24-field state object + a build/validate function; recipes use a `switch (kind.type)` returning bare inputs; the scraper maps a flat RuleField row to a discriminated wire rule. Same shape, three unrelated implementations.

situations.name: Opaque config read-modify-write
situations.definition: Editing one facet of a definition whose settings live in a single serialized JSON blob, without destroying facets the current screen does not render.
situations.note: The bug class is named in a code comment at useScheduleActions.ts:77 — building config from scratch 'silently wipes active_window, rate_limit… turning a business-hours trigger into a 24/7 one with no UI signal'. Every editor re-invents the merge; nothing enforces it.

situations.name: Client mirror of backend rules
situations.definition: Re-implementing a backend evaluation or validation rule in TypeScript so the UI can explain state / give instant feedback without a round trip.
situations.note: Four hand-copied Rust rules, each labelled as such in a comment and each 'kept in sync manually': ActiveWindow::is_active_at, scheduler.rs::next_interval_at, RESERVED_EVENT_TYPES + is_safe_type_string, and EventGateReason::token. Nothing mechanically detects drift.

situations.name: Dry-run preview
situations.definition: Executing a definition's validation and simulated effects without side effects, and rendering what WOULD have happened.
situations.note: Three unrelated result shapes: trigger dry-run returns checks + simulated event + matched subscriptions; scraper preview returns per-URL field/no-match rows; the suggestion flow uses dry-run as a *gate* (create-disabled → dry-run → rollback on fail) rather than a display.

situations.name: Manual test fire
situations.definition: A button that runs a saved automation once, right now, and reports pass/fail + cost + duration inline.
situations.note: Five different result lifecycles: `{ok,data,error}` tuple, a keyed map with a 15s auto-dismiss timer, a run-id-correlated two-phase (render then LLM) runner, an inline result card, and a toast. Only useScheduleActions checks the budget gate first.

situations.name: Connector readiness gating
situations.definition: Deciding whether the user has the credentials a definition needs, and blocking / degrading / annotating the adopt path accordingly.
situations.note: FIVE independent verdicts over the same question: a 0-100 category score, a ready/ambiguous/missing gap report, a 3-state eligible/adoptable-with-setup/incompatible resolver, a block/auto-answer/filter matcher, and the backend-authoritative ready/missing/unknown map. Only the last treats 'unknown' as first-class.

situations.name: Credential-to-slot matching
situations.definition: Resolving 'the template asks for connector X' against 'the vault holds credential with service_type Y' across aliases, categories and creator-path spelling drift.
situations.note: A hand-maintained SERVICE_TYPE_ALIASES table plus prefix/substring heuristics in credentialGapAnalysis (`connector.name.length >= 4 && startsWith`) — a wrong match silently binds the wrong credential to a live automation.

situations.name: Adoption questionnaire
situations.definition: Walking a user through a generated set of questions that parameterize a template, then projecting the answers into a concrete definition.
situations.note: Three unrelated question models — TransformQuestionResponse (categories, dynamic_source, vault_category), PresetParameterOverrides (per-role override map), RecipeBinding (kind union). The blocked/answered interaction is subtle (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:61 subtracts answered from blocked).

situations.name: Connector-sourced option list
situations.definition: Populating a picker's options by calling the user's own connected service at render time, including chained pickers that depend on a prior answer.
situations.note: One hook does this properly (three source kinds, depends_on chaining, no_credential vs fetch_failed error kinds, fingerprint-gated refetch) while the recipe adoption modal hand-rolls the SAME pickers — slack-channel, github-repo, google-calendar — as plain text inputs marked DEFERRED.

situations.name: Multi-step wizard shell
situations.definition: A guided flow with a step rail, per-step completeness, back/next gating, and (sometimes) resumption after the app is closed mid-flow.
situations.note: Ranges from `useState(0)` + a STEPS array (scraper) to a 4-reducer composition with slide direction, session persistence and background snapshot recovery (n8n). No shared stepper, footer, or step-completeness contract.

situations.name: Foreign definition import
situations.definition: Accepting an automation definition authored elsewhere — via file drop, paste, or URL — validating it, and previewing what was detected before committing.
situations.note: useUrlImport does a raw browser `fetch` of a user-supplied URL with a 15s timeout and 5MB cap — no host allowlist, and the same three-path (file/paste/url) validation ladder is re-implemented per path. The batch-template file upload sniffs format with a regex.

situations.name: Streaming generation session
situations.definition: Driving a long backend/LLM job from the UI with live log lines, phase transitions, cancellation, and recovery if the view unmounts or the app restarts.
situations.note: n8n has the full stack (push events + polling fallback + persisted context + session-lost handling); recipe versioning and the design runner each re-derive progress/ETA and terminal expansion locally. The cleanup-dependency trap is documented at RecipeVersionsTab.tsx:56.

situations.name: Definition version history
situations.definition: Generating a new version of a saved definition, previewing the diff/summary, accepting or discarding it, and reverting to an earlier one.
situations.note: The optimistic-lock token (`expectedUpdatedAt` captured before a ~30s generation) exists in exactly one place; the separate staleness check compares an adoption-pinned version to the catalog version with a hand-rolled semver compare. No shared 'is my base still current?' primitive.

situations.name: Raw definition JSON editor
situations.definition: Letting a power user edit the underlying JSON of a definition directly, with syntax highlighting, shape validation, and a safe path back to the structured form.
situations.note: DraftJsonTab hand-builds a highlight-overlay editor (pre + transparent textarea + scroll sync + hljs sanitization); TestTab does a bare textarea + parse-validity gate. TestTab.tsx:196 records the exact bug this prevents — invalid JSON was silently dropped and reported as a successful publish.

situations.name: Route composer
situations.definition: An authoring surface for source→target wiring: arm a source, arm a target, set a run condition, then commit the pending link as a real backend object.
situations.note: Deliberately NOT a node-graph canvas (a retired Builder is referenced in the header comment). The subtlety is two commit paths — direct chain-trigger vs 'configure through the real form locked to a type' — plus a commitBlocker() that says *why* a link isn't committable yet.

situations.name: Definition flow visualization
situations.definition: Rendering a saved or generated automation as a read-only diagram/pipeline so a user can grasp its shape before adopting it.
situations.note: Five renderers for 'show me the shape of this automation', each with its own node model and its own layout math — PresetGraphAdapter's header comment explicitly justifies duplicating ~30 lines rather than adapting the runtime graph component.

situations.name: Untrusted generated definition
situations.definition: Rendering or editing a definition an LLM produced, whose declared TypeScript type is an assertion rather than a guarantee — missing arrays, duplicate ids, wrong enum values, unparseable JSON.
situations.note: Each site re-derives its own defensive read: dedupe-nodes-by-id with a DEV warn, a mirrored normalization in the modal that wraps it, per-field String()/typeof coercion of `unknown[]`, silent try/catch returning []. useCreateTemplateSnapshot.ts:25 additionally scrubs secret-looking fragments before sending a malformed sample to Sentry — nobody else does.

situations.name: Unsaved draft persistence
situations.definition: Keeping in-progress authoring work alive across a remount, a route change, or an app restart — and deciding when it is too stale to restore.
situations.note: Three storage strategies coexist — versioned localStorage with a token-migration pass, a maxAge-validated persisted context hook, and module-level mutable globals (useStructuredQuery.ts:39) that also need a rehydrate-the-parent effect to avoid showing filters that aren't applied.

situations.name: Idempotent adopt
situations.definition: Committing a catalog item onto a persona exactly once, surviving double-clicks and stale UI, with honest reporting when a follow-up step partially fails.
situations.note: Three different dedupe strategies — dedupe inside a queued mutator, a synchronous re-entrancy ref plus backend single-flight, and create→dry-run→delete-on-failure rollback. Each also invents its own 'succeeded but partially' toast (param-sync failed / coverage gap / handoff not wired).

situations.name: Partial-success bulk action
situations.definition: Applying an action to many selected items and reporting per-reason failure counts rather than a single success/fail.
situations.note: Four incompatible outcome types for the same idea — BulkDeadLetterOutcome{succeeded,failed[reason]}, AdoptedTeamPresetResult{failed_members[role,reason]}, BulkActionResult[] counted by PromiseSettled fulfilled/rejected, BackfillResult{slotsEnqueued,failures,capped} — each with its own selection-reconciliation after the write.

situations.name: Dead-letter triage
situations.definition: Reviewing events that failed terminally, clustering them by failure mode, and retrying or discarding them under a retry cap.
situations.note: Low recurrence, high consequence: a client-side Jaccard clusterer with an eyeballed 0.55 threshold decides which failures look alike, and the retry cap is fetched from the backend with a hardcoded fallback so labels can't drift from MAX_MANUAL_RETRIES.

situations.name: Webhook request inspector
situations.definition: Showing the raw inbound requests an endpoint received, with headers/body, the resulting event, and replay / copy-as-cURL affordances.
situations.note: Headers are rendered verbatim in a JSON block — a replayable log of signed inbound requests is a secret-exposure surface with no redaction layer. The infinite-refetch trap (empty result treated as never-fetched) is documented at line 183.

situations.name: Inbound secret provisioning
situations.definition: Generating, displaying, and letting the user rotate the shared secret that authenticates an inbound webhook.
situations.note: Local webhooks auto-generate a 32-byte HMAC secret in a form-serialization helper; the cloud path creates a webhook trigger with `{event_type:'webhook'}` and no secret at all. Same user-facing concept, incompatible security posture.

situations.name: Natural-language to definition
situations.definition: Turning a sentence the user typed into a pre-filled structured definition, with confidence and honest disclosure of anything the parser rewrote.
situations.note: One is a regex rule table with a first-match-wins loop and an explicit NlParseWarning channel (added because silent interval clamping was 'Success Theater'); the other calls an LLM to synthesize scrape rules. Neither shares a 'parsed → apply to form' contract — TriggerAddForm.tsx:125 hand-copies 18 fields.

situations.name: Rate-limit controls
situations.definition: Authoring throttle policy (max per window, cooldown, max concurrent) and showing the live runtime state against it.
situations.note: Editing the policy and observing it are in two different surfaces with two different state sources (config blob vs TriggerRateLimitState store slice); a policy is only meaningful next to its live counters.

situations.name: Blast-radius confirmation
situations.definition: Confirming a destructive or wide-reaching change by first telling the user exactly how many live things it will touch.
situations.owner: src/features/shared/components/overlays/ConfirmDestructiveModal.tsx (used by one caller in this slice)
situations.note: The shared primitive already has a `blastRadius` slot and a `requireTypedConfirmation` gate (ConfirmDestructiveModal.tsx:19) — but in this slice only DeadLetterTab uses it, and without blastRadius. RenameEventDialog carries affectedCounts by hand; SmeeRelayTab hand-rolls a two-button inline confirm with no impact statement at all.

situations.name: Live event console
situations.definition: A continuously-updating stream view of system events with pause/resume buffering, a bounded window, and per-row detail.
situations.note: The hard parts are all backpressure: rAF-batched ingest, a 200-row buffer with index eviction, a 10k timestamp cap for the events/min window, a paused replay queue, and rejecting lightweight CDC notifications multiplexed on the same channel.

situations.name: Schedule calendar
situations.definition: Laying fleet-wide schedule fires onto a week/month grid, distinguishing projected future fires from real past outcomes, and flagging overlaps.
situations.note: The doctrine here is worth codifying: past slots are matched to REAL run records and unmatched ones render 'past-unknown' rather than a fabricated success. Performance is delicate — a value-signature dep key exists because identity-keying re-fired 500-slot IPCs per poll.

situations.name: Backfill window picker
situations.definition: Letting a user replay missed schedule fires over an explicit time window, with caps, future clipping, and a report of what was enqueued.
situations.note: Two distinct catch-up concepts with unrelated UIs — an automatic `max_backfill` <select> in the trigger authoring form and a manual [start,end] replay modal. Both can enqueue up to 100 real executions; only the modal shows a cost-shaped preview.

situations.name: Local/remote reconcile
situations.definition: Detecting that a remote-side object exists without a local record (or vice versa) and offering adopt / destroy / dismiss per item.
situations.note: Orphaned cloud deployments are still billing; the banner is deliberately read-only until the user acts. The catalog-staleness case is the same shape (pinned version vs current) but presented as a passive chip with no adopt/discard path.

situations.name: Catalog browse and compare
situations.definition: Searching a large definition catalog with structured/faceted filters and putting two or more candidates side by side before choosing.
situations.note: The gallery has a `category:`/`difficulty:`/`setup:` chip DSL, a compare tray, and virtualization; the recipes and explore catalogs re-implement browse from scratch. buildComparison.ts is the good pattern — it reuses the card's own cached parse so compare can't disagree with a card.

situations.name: Quick-start palette
situations.definition: Offering a curated set of pre-filled starting points (templates, presets, quick ranges, canned test cases) that seed a form instead of starting blank.
situations.note: Every palette is a local `as const` array with its own shape and its own apply-to-form function (TriggerAddForm.tsx:106 hand-maps template config back into 6 setState calls, and silently ignores template kinds it doesn't handle).

situations.name: Per-row async action state
situations.definition: Tracking which row of a list currently has an action in flight, and where its transient result renders.
situations.note: Six encodings of the same state: `Record<id,{running,result}>` with dismiss timers, `Set<id>` with start/end helpers, a busy-`Set` wrapper, a nullable `replayingId` + result-with-id, a per-row `useSubscribeToggle` busy lock, and an `exitingIds` set driving exit animation. Only one clears its timers on unmount; the double-click race is re-solved locally each time.

situations.name: Marketplace feed wiring
situations.definition: Turning a subscribed external feed into a live listener on a persona.
situations.note: Subscription and wiring live in different tabs; the bridge is a naming convention (`shared:<slug>` bus events) encoded in one branch of studioCommit with no shared constant.

situations.name: Multi-modal stack
situations.definition: Managing several stacked overlays from one surface without a useState pair per modal.
situations.note: Already-documented (Modals) — noting recurrence only. A good typed stack primitive exists in the gallery but nothing outside it uses it; StudioPatchbay keeps 5 independent nullable modal states and FrequencyEditor hand-rolls `fixed inset-0` despite the enforce-base-modal rule.

situations.name: Definition list tables
situations.definition: Listing triggers / schedules / deployments / recipes with loading, empty, and filter states.
situations.note: Already-documented (Tables) — noting recurrence only. LiveStreamTab uses DataGrid properly; DeadLetterTab and PreviewResults hand-roll rows.

situations.name: Section cold-load states
situations.definition: First-paint behaviour for async panels in these tabs — ghost rows, delayed skeletons, empty-vs-loading disambiguation.
situations.note: Already-documented (Page loading) — noting recurrence only. useConnectorReadiness explicitly cites law 1 (a refetch keeps serving previous verdicts); RecipeVersionsTab still does a bare `loading ? spinner`.
